extracted.intended_audience: Authors (early-career and experienced researchers) preparing manuscript revisions and responses to peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on preparing response letters and revising manuscripts in reaction to peer review comments, including handling ambiguous or ethical situations and organizing revisions clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling requests for non-citation of specific authors
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers request that specific authors not be cited due to reputational concerns or prior behavior, evaluate whether the request pertains to the author as an individual or to the research itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request is rooted in personal or ethical concerns, authors should consider discreetly contacting the editor for guidance. Determine whether the issue relates to the work's validity or to the individual's reputation; treat them differently. Be aware of the increasing prominence of post-publication peer review platforms (PubPeer, ScienceOpen, PREreview) that may make such situations more common. Aim to preserve fairness, transparency, and ethical treatment of manuscripts when responding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledging reviewers in the acknowledgements section
rubrics_metrics.description: Include reviewers in the acknowledgements section of the article when their feedback has substantially contributed to improving the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond thanking reviewers in the response letter, formally recognizing reviewers in the article's acknowledgements 'demonstrates appreciation beyond the response letter' and 'cultivates positive relationships' by acknowledging underappreciated labor. Add a clear note only when reviewers' feedback substantially improved the work; follow journal policies about anonymous vs. named acknowledgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid copying reviewers' comments into the manuscript (no plagiarism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not directly copy and paste reviewers' comments into the manuscript; paraphrase and integrate reviewers' suggestions using the author's own words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To uphold scholarly integrity, 'it is essential to avoid directly copying and pasting reviewers' comments into the manuscript.' Instead, paraphrase reviewer suggestions and incorporate them as original prose. Anti-pattern: inserting verbatim reviewer text (example cited of nearly a full page copied verbatim). Emphasize originality when integrating feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce redundancies and repetition for clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Streamline sections by consolidating similar points to eliminate repeated statements (e.g., repeated comments about professionalism or responding to reviewers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove redundant passages to improve flow and readability; consolidate overlapping advice into single clear statements. This makes the manuscript more concise and engaging and helps readers locate guidance more easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain professionalism and constructive tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a balanced approach that combines firmness in defending one’s scholarly contributions with openness to constructive feedback, promoting respectful and cooperative dynamics between authors and reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistently emphasize professionalism in responses and revisions. Use a constructive tone in the response letter, avoid personal attacks, and treat reviewers' critiques as opportunities to improve the manuscript. This principle underpins trust and transparency in the peer review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical organization with clear headings and subheadings
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure the manuscript and guidance with well-defined headings and subheadings to aid readability and navigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear section structuring 'greatly aids readability' and helps readers find relevant information. Use headings/subheadings to separate topics (e.g., Tips, Ambiguous Situations, Ethical Considerations, Responding to Reviewers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Break down complex reviewer comments and address each point methodically
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewer comments are complex, decompose them into manageable parts and address each component methodically in the response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice includes parsing multi-part critiques into numbered items and responding to each. This demystifies the revision process and helps ensure no element is missed. Use clear markers in the response letter (e.g., 'Comment 1', 'Author response') so reviewers and editors can track changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to every point raised
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay attention to details and ensure the response letter addresses every comment made by reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly respond to all reviewer points (even when declining a suggestion), explaining the action taken or providing a reasoned rebuttal. The section 'Pay attention to details: Respond to every point raised' emphasizes this as central to good revision practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tables to organize responses to reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ tables to present reviewer comments, author responses, and manuscript changes in a clear, organized format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables allow a concise mapping of each comment to the specific revision and location in the manuscript, making it easier for editors and reviewers to verify changes. The reviewer endorses 'The suggestion to use tables to organize responses to reviewers is excellent.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek guidance from editors or mentors when unsure
rubrics_metrics.description: If unsure how to address a particular comment or when reviewer requests conflict with journal guidelines, consult the editor or a mentor for guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical step: 'If an author is unsure how to address a particular comment, they can reach out to the editor or a mentor for guidance.' When requests conflict with journal policy, discreet editorial consultation helps find an acceptable solution. Document any editorial advice in your response if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize feedback and distinguish major vs minor comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop strategies to prioritize which reviewer suggestions are major (affecting conclusions/methods) versus minor (stylistic/clarifying), and provide examples to illustrate these distinctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete examples of major vs. minor comments to guide authors. Focus effort on substantive changes that affect validity, robustness, or interpretation; minor edits can be listed and handled succinctly. State priorities clearly in the cover letter or response where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference relevant ethical guidelines and journal policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen ethical considerations by citing specific guidelines or policies (e.g., COPE) that journals or organizations have for handling ethical or ambiguous situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point authors to authoritative resources (Committee on Publication Ethics, journal-specific policies) when discussing plagiarism, conflicts of interest, requests to omit citations, or other ethical dilemmas. Explicit referencing provides a clearer path for authors to follow and demonstrates adherence to community standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance respecting reviewers' suggestions with authors' vision
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewers' requests conflict with the authors' original vision or journal guidelines, negotiate solutions that respect both reviewer input and the integrity of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, simplify recommendations, provide reasoned rebuttals, or seek editorial approval for substantive disagreements. Explain why certain suggestions were not adopted and offer alternative changes where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express gratitude to reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Thank reviewers for their time and thoughtful feedback in the response letter and consider reiterating gratitude in the manuscript where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge reviewers' contributions in the response and—if their feedback substantially improved the work—consider a note in the acknowledgements section. Re-stating appreciation fosters goodwill and acknowledges peer labor.
